intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Day Trip
experiences.description: Hop between the stunning Phi Phi islands by longtail boat, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Viking Cave, and relaxing on pristine white sand beaches made famous by 'The Beach'. Includes snorkeling gear and a traditional Thai lunch on board.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the legendary Yaowarat Road Chinatown and Khao San Road area sampling iconic Thai street food including pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, tom yum soup, and fresh coconut ice cream. Join a guided walking tour to discover hidden food stalls locals love.

experiences.name: Similan Islands Snorkeling & Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a speedboat to the world-renowned Similan Islands, a protected national park featuring some of Southeast Asia's most spectacular coral reefs, exotic marine life, and powdery white beaches. Snorkel alongside sea turtles, reef sharks, and vibrant tropical fish in turquoise waters.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Island Hopping by Longtail Boat
experiences.description: Explore the laid-back southern islands around Koh Lanta including Koh Rok and Koh Haa, known for their untouched beaches, dramatic limestone caves, and vibrant underwater ecosystems. Enjoy a fresh seafood lunch on a secluded beach and watch the sunset paint the Andaman Sea orange.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Sunday Night Bazaar Street Food Crawl
experiences.description: Explore the famous Sunday Walking Street in the Old City of Chiang Mai, tasting northern Thai specialties like khao soi (coconut curry noodle soup), sai oua (northern Thai sausage), and crispy pork rinds. Browse handmade crafts and enjoy live traditional music performances as you eat your way through the market.
experiences.location: Wualai Road, Old City, Chiang Mai

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange onward transport to Phi Phi Islands. Take a budget shared minivan or bus to Rassada Pier in Phuket or Ao Nang Pier in Krabi (depending on routing). Purchase ferry ticket to Phi Phi Don Island (approximately 300-450 THB). Board afternoon ferry and enjoy scenic views of the Andaman Sea on the 1.5-2 hour crossing.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phi Phi Don, check into your boutique stay. Take a leisurely stroll along the Tonsai Bay beachfront to get your bearings. Explore the lively Tonsai Village walking street and night market area. Watch the sunset from the beach if timing allows.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport (budget 80-150 THB)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick pad thai or fried rice from an airport food court or pier-side street stall (100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village street food stalls - try grilled satay skewers, papaya salad, and sticky rice. Look for local Thai restaurants away from the main tourist strip for cheaper prices (150-200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some currency at the airport for better rates than on the island. Carry small bills for street food. The ferry schedule from Phuket/Krabi to Phi Phi typically has afternoon departures around 14:30-15:30, so timing should work well.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to Phi Phi Viewpoint (30-minute uphill trek, entrance fee ~30 THB). Arrive before 8:00 AM to beat crowds and enjoy panoramic views of the twin bays and surrounding islands in the morning light. Take photos and soak in the scenery before descending back to the village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Long Beach (Haad Yao) on the eastern side of Phi Phi Don - reachable by a 20-minute walk or cheap longtail boat (50 THB). Spend the afternoon swimming and snorkeling in the clear turquoise water. Long Beach is less crowded than Tonsai Bay and has beautiful coral near the shore. Rent basic snorkel gear from a beach shack (50-80 THB/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and explore the night market. Watch fire show performances on the beach (free to watch, tip the performers). Browse cheap souvenirs and local crafts along the walking street.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie and banana pancake from a street vendor near the pier area (60-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside coconut with fresh fruit or a simple fried rice from a Long Beach shack restaurant (100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Night market street food feast - try mango sticky rice, grilled corn, and a bowl of tom yum soup from different stalls (150-200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: October is shoulder season and can bring occasional rain showers. Carry a light rain poncho. The viewpoint hike is best done early morning or late afternoon to avoid heat. Stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling day trip departing from Tonsai Pier around 8:30 AM. Book through a local guesthouse or pier-side agent for the best rates (600-900 THB for a full-day longtail boat trip). Visit Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh (made famous by The Beach film) - note that swimming inside the bay may be restricted for reef conservation, but the surrounding waters are stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping trip to Pileh Lagoon (a stunning emerald-green enclosed lagoon), Viking Cave (with ancient cave paintings and swallow nests), and Loh Samah Bay for snorkeling among colorful fish and coral. The boat typically returns to Tonsai around 16:00-17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and freshen up at the guesthouse. Take an evening walk to the quieter Loh Dalum Bay on the north side of the island to watch the sunset over the bay. Browse the beachfront bars for cheap happy hour drinks.

meals.breakfast: Simple toast with eggs and coffee from a small local café near the guesthouse (80-120 THB)
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included in the boat trip package or buy simple sandwiches and snacks to bring onboard (50-100 THB extra)
meals.dinner: Try a local Thai restaurant set back from the beach - order green curry with rice or pad see ew. Look for places with Thai script menus for authentic and cheaper prices (120-180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor hours and swimming zones due to reef restoration efforts. Confirm current rules with your tour operator. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and underwater camera or waterproof phone case.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak from the beach (200-300 THB for 2 hours) and paddle around the northern coastline of Phi Phi Don at your own pace. Explore hidden coves, small caves, and quiet beaches inaccessible by foot. The morning light on the limestone cliffs is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Phi Phi Natural Education Center (free entry) to learn about the 2004 tsunami impact and the island's recovery and conservation efforts. Spend the later afternoon relaxing on Tonsai Bay beach, swimming in the warm Andaman water, and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Loh Dalum Bay for the evening. This bay transforms into a lively social scene at night. Enjoy a cheap local beer (Chang or Singha, 60-80 THB) while sitting on the beach. Watch the fire dancers perform on the sand.

meals.breakfast: Coconut pancakes and fresh-pressed orange juice from a beachside breakfast spot (80-120 THB)
meals.lunch: Street food pad thai made fresh in a wok at a Tonsai Village stall - watch it being cooked in front of you (80-120 THB)
meals.dinner: Grilled seafood skewers and som tam (papaya salad) from the night market. Share dishes to try more variety and save money (150-200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking is best done in the morning when the sea is calmer. Avoid paddling too far from shore if you are not an experienced kayaker. October seas can occasionally be choppy due to monsoon season transitions.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approximately 250-350 THB, 1.5-2 hours). Arrive in Krabi and store luggage at the pier or a guesthouse. Explore Krabi Town's morning market (Talat Kao) for an authentic local experience - browse fresh produce, local snacks, and cheap breakfast options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Tham Seua (Tiger Cave Temple) - a famous temple complex about 3 km from Krabi Town (accessible by songthaew for 30-50 THB). Climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for incredible panoramic views of Krabi's karst landscape and coastline. The climb takes about 45-60 minutes each way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town and explore the Chao Fah Pier Walking Street night market (open Thursday-Sunday, check current schedule). If the market is open, it is one of the best budget food spots in Krabi with dozens of local vendors. Check into a budget guesthouse in Krabi Town for the night.

meals.breakfast: Khao tom (rice soup) or jok (congee) with a fried egg at the Krabi Town morning market - authentic Thai breakfast (50-80 THB)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Tiger Cave Temple - simple rice dishes with curries or stir-fries (80-120 THB)
meals.dinner: Chao Fah Walking Street market - try rotee (Thai crepes), grilled meats, fresh spring rolls, and local desserts (150-200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple summit climb is physically demanding - wear comfortable shoes, carry water, and avoid midday heat. The views at the top are absolutely worth the effort. Dress modestly as it is a religious site (cover shoulders and knees).

day_by_day.morning: Take a songthaew from Krabi Town to Ao Nang Beach (30-40 THB, 30 minutes). Explore the Ao Nang beachfront and browse the many tour operators for the best deals on island-hopping longtail boat trips. Arrange a shared longtail boat to the Four Islands (Koh Mor, Koh Tub, Koh Chicken, and Koh Poda) for approximately 600-800 THB per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon island-hopping among the Four Islands. Koh Poda has a beautiful white sand beach with crystal-clear water. Koh Tub and Koh Mor are connected by a sandbar at low tide - walk between them for a unique experience. Snorkel at Koh Chicken which has good coral and marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang by longtail boat around 17:00. Explore the Ao Nang evening market and beachfront restaurants. Watch the sunset over the Andaman Sea from Ao Nang Beach. Take a songthaew back to Krabi Town for the night.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast in Krabi Town before heading to Ao Nang - fresh fruit, toast, and coffee from a local café (80-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the boat trip, or buy simple food from beach vendors on Koh Poda (100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang beachfront street food area - try fresh grilled fish, som tam, and khao niao (sticky rice) before heading back to Krabi Town (150-200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Four Islands trip directly with longtail boat operators at the Ao Nang pier rather than through hotel desks for better prices. Negotiate for group rates if traveling with others. Bring cash as remote islands do not have ATMs.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (100 THB, 15 minutes - Railay is only accessible by boat as it is surrounded by cliffs). Explore East Railay and West Railay beaches. Hike the short jungle trail between the two beaches. Visit the famous Phra Nang Cave on Phra Nang Beach, a sacred shrine adorned with colorful offerings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to the Railay Viewpoint for panoramic views of the peninsula and surrounding sea (challenging 30-minute scramble up limestone rocks using ropes). Alternatively, rent snorkel gear and explore the coral around Phra Nang Beach. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on the stunning Phra Nang Beach, consistently rated one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Take the longtail boat back to Ao Nang before dark (last boats around 18:00-19:00). Head back to Krabi Town for the evening. Visit the riverside promenade along the Krabi River for a relaxing evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang street food breakfast - roti with banana and condensed milk, a classic Thai breakfast treat (60-80 THB)
meals.lunch: Railay Beach has some restaurants but they are pricier due to the remote location - bring packed snacks or budget for a simple rice dish (150-200 THB on Railay)
meals.dinner: Back in Krabi Town - find a local Thai restaurant serving khao pad (fried rice) or massaman curry with roti (100-150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is one of Thailand's most scenic spots. The longtail boats from Ao Nang run frequently throughout the day. Be aware that boats may not run in rough weather. Wear water shoes as the boat landing can be wet and rocky.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus or minivan from Krabi Town to Koh Lanta (approximately 300-400 THB including ferry crossings, 2-2.5 hours). Check into a budget guesthouse or bungalow on Long Beach (Haad Phra Ae), one of Koh Lanta's most popular and beautiful beaches. Drop off bags and head straight to the beach for a swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a motorbike (150-200 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta at your own pace. Drive south along the west coast road, stopping at Klong Khong Beach, Klong Nin Beach, and Kantiang Bay. Each beach has a distinct character. Continue to the southern tip to visit Koh Lanta National Park (200 THB entrance fee) and its lighthouse with stunning views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach for the sunset - Koh Lanta sunsets are spectacular with unobstructed western views. Browse the low-key beachfront restaurants and bars along Long Beach for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Eat before leaving Krabi Town - grab a local breakfast from a market stall (60-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Simple beachside restaurant on Klong Nin Beach during the motorbike tour - fresh fish or chicken with rice (120-160 THB)
meals.dinner: Long Beach beachfront restaurant - order grilled barracuda or red snapper with steamed rice and a fresh lime soda. Many restaurants have happy hour deals (200-300 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less crowded than Phi Phi, making it perfect for budget travelers seeking a quieter island experience. October is the tail end of the rainy season on Koh Lanta, so expect some afternoon showers. The national park is worth the entrance fee for the scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) on the eastern coast of the island by motorbike (20-minute ride from Long Beach). This charming old fishing village has colorful wooden shophouses built on stilts over the water, Chinese temples, and a laid-back atmosphere. Explore the narrow streets and visit the local market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget snorkeling trip to the surrounding smaller islands - Koh Rok or the Koh Ha group are popular choices with excellent visibility and coral (book through local operators for 800-1,200 THB for a full-day shared trip). These islands have some of the best snorkeling in the Krabi region with diverse marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach for the evening. Explore the weekly night market if it coincides with your visit (check local schedule). Otherwise, enjoy a quiet beachside dinner watching the stars over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Old Town morning coffee and local Thai sweets from a Chinese-Thai café in Ban Si Raya (60-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Lunch included with most island snorkeling tours, or bring your own packed food to save money (50-100 THB extra if not included)
meals.dinner: Beachside barbecue restaurant on Long Beach - many offer set meals with grilled seafood, salad, and rice at reasonable prices (200-250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok and Koh Ha are protected marine areas with strict no-touching-coral rules. The snorkeling here is genuinely world-class. Book tours the evening before to secure spots and potentially negotiate better group rates.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxing morning on Long Beach - swim, read, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before the daily tourist boats arrive. Take a morning yoga class if available at one of the beachside bungalow resorts (some offer free or donation-based classes). Explore the mangrove area at the northern end of Long Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry and connecting transport from Koh Lanta back toward the Phuket area (approximately 400-600 THB, 3-4 hours total journey). Arrive in Phuket and check into a budget guesthouse in Patong or Kata Beach area. Freshen up and explore the local area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Patong Beach in the evening. Walk along the beachfront promenade and browse the cheap shopping stalls along Bangla Road. Enjoy the vibrant street food scene around the Patong area without necessarily spending money at the tourist-priced restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit bowl and yogurt from a Long Beach café before departing (80-120 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the ferry journey or eat at the pier restaurant in Koh Lanta before boarding (100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Patong night market or local Thai restaurant away from the main Bangla Road tourist strip - try a bowl of boat noodles or pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) (100-150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The journey from Koh Lanta to Phuket involves a combination of ferry and minivan - book through a travel agent in Koh Lanta for a seamless connection. Travel times can vary with weather conditions in October.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or songthaew from Patong to Phuket Town (25-30 THB, 30 minutes). Explore the charming Sino-Portuguese old town with its colorful heritage buildings, street art murals, and ornate Chinese shrines. Walk along Thalang Road, Soi Rommanee, and Dibuk Road to see the best-preserved architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the weekend market at Chillva Market or Phuket Walking Street (Lard Yai) if it falls on a Sunday (check schedule). Browse local handicrafts, clothing, and street food at very affordable prices. Alternatively, visit Wat Chalong (free entry, donations welcome), Phuket's most important Buddhist temple, a 20-minute songthaew ride from town.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach area for the evening. Head to Kata Beach or Karon Beach for a more relaxed and less commercial atmosphere than Patong. Watch the sunset from the beach and enjoy a quiet evening meal.

meals.breakfast: Phuket Town's famous local breakfast - try khanom jeen (fermented rice noodles with curry sauce) or dim sum from a Chinese-Thai coffee shop (60-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Phuket Town local restaurant - try Phuket-style hokkien noodles or mee sua (thin noodle soup), a local specialty unique to Phuket (80-120 THB)
meals.dinner: Kata Beach area - find a local Thai restaurant serving fresh seafood at market prices. Avoid the overpriced tourist restaurants on the beachfront itself (200-280 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is a UNESCO-recognized heritage area and genuinely fascinating to explore on foot. The Sino-Portuguese architecture dates from the tin mining boom of the 19th century. Many cafés and shops have opened in restored heritage buildings - worth a browse even on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Phang Nga Bay by joining a budget group tour (600-900 THB). Depart from Phuket by minivan to Phang Nga Bay pier, then take a longtail boat through the mangrove-lined bay. Visit the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), made famous in The Man with the Golden Gun. Marvel at the towering limestone karst formations rising from the emerald water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Phang Nga Bay tour visiting sea caves and hongs (hidden lagoons inside limestone islands accessible only by kayak or longtail at low tide). Visit a floating Muslim fishing village (Ko Panyi) for lunch and to see this unique community built entirely on stilts over the water. Return to Phuket by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Phuket area. Visit the Phuket Night Bazaar or a local market for last-minute souvenir shopping at budget prices. Enjoy a farewell Thai street food dinner with all your favorite dishes from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before the early tour departure - grab something from a 7-Eleven or local stall near the guesthouse (60-80 THB)
meals.lunch: Ko Panyi floating village - fresh seafood lunch at the village restaurants. The seafood is fresh and reasonably priced given the location (150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food farewell dinner - order all your trip favorites: pad thai, som tam, satay, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut. Visit multiple stalls to try everything (200-250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay is absolutely stunning and one of Thailand's most iconic landscapes. Book the tour through a local agent rather than a hotel desk for better prices. Some tours include kayaking through sea caves which is a highlight - confirm what is included before booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a leisurely last breakfast in Phuket. Take a final walk on the beach to collect memories. Visit a local market one last time to pick up any remaining souvenirs - dried fruits, Thai spices, local snacks, and handicrafts make great budget-friendly gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation and arrange transport to Phuket International Airport (metered taxi approximately 400-500 THB from Patong, or shared minivan for 150-200 THB). Allow plenty of time for airport check-in, immigration, and security. Browse the airport duty-free for any last purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Thailand with incredible memories of stunning beaches, vibrant street food, and island adventures. Reflect on the amazing experiences of 13 days exploring the best of southern Thailand on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast - try khao tom (rice porridge) with ginger and century egg, a comforting classic (60-100 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport food court for a final Thai meal before departure - most airports have reasonably priced local food options in the pre-security area (150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Airplane meal or purchase food at the airport if departure is in the evening

day_by_day.notes: Budget approximately 150-200 THB per person for airport transfer by shared minivan. Keep some Thai baht for any last-minute expenses. Remember to save enough local currency for the taxi or transport to the airport. Total estimated daily food budget throughout the trip: 400-650 THB per day (approximately 11-18 USD). Accommodation in budget guesthouses and bungalows: 400-800 THB per night. Activities and transport: 500-1,200 THB per day.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and take a shared shuttle or taxi to Rassada Pier in Phuket Town, then board a ferry to Phi Phi Don Island (approx. 1.5–2 hour journey). Check in to your boutique stay and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Village to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village walking street. Browse local shops and soak in the island atmosphere as the sun sets over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at the airport before or after landing — try a Thai rice bowl or pad kra pao at an airport food court stall (approx. 80–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Skip or grab light bites on the ferry (packaged snacks available on board).
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant on Tonsai Village — a mid-range local favourite serving authentic Thai dishes like massaman curry and fresh seafood. Budget approx. 200–350 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance online or at the pier. Arrive at Rassada Pier at least 30 minutes before departure. October may bring occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket. Keep cash handy as some island vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (approximately 20–30 minute uphill walk from Tonsai Village). Enjoy the breathtaking panoramic view of both bays at sunrise. The hike is moderate — wear good shoes and bring water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back down and rent a kayak or join a short longtail boat trip to Loh Dalum Bay. Spend the afternoon swimming and snorkelling in the crystal-clear turquoise waters. Explore the shallow reef near the bay's edges.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village and wander the night market along the main walking street. Watch fire shows on the beach — a Phi Phi signature experience.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a fresh fruit platter, toast, and coffee at your boutique hotel or a nearby café like Ciao Bella Café (approx. 120–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh coconut and a grilled satay skewer from a beach vendor, or eat at a casual beachside restaurant (approx. 150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Unni's Restaurant — a beloved spot on Phi Phi serving Thai and international dishes. Try the green curry or pad thai. Budget approx. 200–400 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: The viewpoint hike is best done before 8:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds. Bring sunscreen and insect repellent. October weather may be partly cloudy but the views are still spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Join a half-day snorkelling tour around Phi Phi's surrounding islands — typically includes stops at Shark Point, Mosquito Island, and Pileh Lagoon. Longtail boat tours depart from Tonsai pier from around 8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the tour and relax on Loh Dalum Beach. Rent a sun lounger and enjoy the calm waters. Alternatively, explore the quieter Long Beach on the south side of Phi Phi Don by longtail (10-minute ride).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar or beachfront spot. Enjoy the golden hour views and a refreshing cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the tour — try a local Thai breakfast of jok (rice porridge) or khao tom from a street stall near Tonsai pier (approx. 60–100 THB).
meals.lunch: Most snorkelling tours include a simple lunch on a beach stop — fresh fruit, rice, and grilled fish. Confirm with your tour operator.
meals.dinner: Local Street Food Night — explore the Tonsai walking street stalls for pad kra pao, mango sticky rice, and grilled corn. Budget approx. 150–250 THB for a full street food meal.

day_by_day.notes: Book snorkelling tours the evening before at any tour desk in Tonsai Village. Half-day tours cost approx. 500–800 THB per person. Bring an underwater camera or rent a waterproof phone case.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat to Phi Phi Leh — the uninhabited sister island. Visit the famous Maya Bay (made iconic by 'The Beach'). Arrive early to beat the crowds. Note that Maya Bay has regulated visitor hours — check current rules upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Phi Phi Leh's Viking Cave (view from the boat) and Pileh Lagoon — a stunning enclosed emerald lagoon perfect for swimming. Return to Phi Phi Don by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening at your boutique hotel. Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage at one of the many affordable spas in Tonsai Village (approx. 300–500 THB for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel if included, or visit a bakery café near Tonsai for banana pancakes and coffee (approx. 100–180 THB).
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat a light meal before departing — the longtail tour may not include food. Buy fresh fruit and sandwiches from a Tonsai convenience store.
meals.dinner: Phi Phi Blanco Beach Bar & Restaurant — enjoy fresh grilled seafood with your feet in the sand. Try the whole grilled snapper or tiger prawns. Budget approx. 300–500 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private longtail boat for the day (approx. 1,500–2,500 THB) or join a shared tour. Maya Bay may have entry fees and timed slots — verify current regulations before visiting. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hours). Check in to a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in Krabi Town. Drop your bags and head to the Krabi Town Walking Street Market (if visiting on a weekend) or explore the town centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for a panoramic view of Krabi's limestone karsts and jungle. Allow 1.5–2 hours for the full climb and descent.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Krabi Town riverside promenade and explore the vibrant Night Market on the waterfront. Sample a wide variety of street food from local vendors.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the ferry — grab a quick Thai-style breakfast at a Tonsai stall (approx. 60–100 THB).
meals.lunch: After arriving in Krabi, try a local restaurant near the pier for a classic khao pad (Thai fried rice) or boat noodles (approx. 80–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Krabi Town Night Market — feast on grilled meats, pad thai, som tam (papaya salad), and fresh coconut ice cream. Budget approx. 150–250 THB for a hearty street food dinner.

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes, bring plenty of water, and avoid midday heat. Dress modestly as it is an active temple (shoulders and knees covered). The ferry from Phi Phi to Krabi departs multiple times daily — book the morning slot.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day island hopping tour from Krabi to the famous Four Islands (Koh Mook, Koh Kradan, Koh Ngai, and Koh Cheuk). Depart by longtail boat from Klong Jilad Pier in Krabi. Snorkel at coral reefs and swim in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the tour — visit the stunning Emerald Cave (Tham Morakot) on Koh Mook, accessible only by swimming through a dark sea cave that opens into a hidden beach. A truly magical experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town by late afternoon. Rest and refresh at your hotel before heading out for a relaxed evening along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local coffee shop for toast and eggs (approx. 100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included in Four Islands tour packages — usually a beachside Thai buffet on one of the islands.
meals.dinner: Ruen Mai Restaurant in Krabi Town — a well-regarded local restaurant known for authentic southern Thai cuisine. Try the crab curry or sour curry with vegetables. Budget approx. 200–350 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: Four Islands tours cost approx. 700–1,200 THB per person including lunch. Book through your hotel or a reputable tour desk. The Emerald Cave swim requires confidence in water — life jackets are provided. October seas can be slightly choppy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Krabi's Ao Nang Beach to Railay Beach (approx. 15–20 minute ride) — accessible only by boat. Explore the stunning Railay West and Railay East beaches. Attempt the short but rewarding hike to Railay Viewpoint for panoramic karst views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the mysterious Phra Nang Cave (Princess Cave) on Phra Nang Beach — a sacred cave filled with wooden phallus offerings. Swim and snorkel at Phra Nang Beach, consistently rated one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a longtail back to Ao Nang and enjoy the lively Ao Nang Beach strip. Browse shops and enjoy the buzzing atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi hotel or a café near the pier (approx. 100–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the beachside restaurants on Railay West — try a fresh seafood platter or green curry with rice (approx. 200–350 THB).
meals.dinner: Ao Nang Street Food — the main Ao Nang strip has numerous food stalls and casual restaurants. Try khao man gai (chicken rice) or a freshly grilled fish with sticky rice (approx. 150–300 THB).

day_by_day.notes: Longtail boats to Railay run on demand from Ao Nang Beach (approx. 100–150 THB per person each way). The beach is beautiful but can get crowded by midday — arrive early. Wear water shoes as the boat landing can be rocky.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — take a ferry or speedboat from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Check in to a mid-range beachfront bungalow or resort on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao). Settle in and take a walk along the long, peaceful beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a charming historic fishing village with wooden shophouses, sea gypsy culture, and artisan shops on stilts over the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your beach area and watch the sunset from the beach. Koh Lanta is known for spectacular west-facing sunsets.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before the ferry — or eat on arrival in Koh Lanta at a local café near the pier.
meals.lunch: Old Town café lunch — try a traditional Thai lunch set or fresh seafood at one of the charming wooden restaurants in Ban Ko Lanta (approx. 150–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Time for a Sunset Dinner on the beach — many beachfront restaurants on Long Beach offer tables in the sand. Try the grilled barracuda or massaman lamb curry. Budget approx. 250–400 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Krabi to Koh Lanta run seasonally — confirm availability for October. Scooter rental costs approx. 200–300 THB per day. Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less crowded than Phi Phi — a perfect mid-trip change of pace.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day snorkelling and island hopping tour around the Koh Lanta Marine National Park. Visit Koh Rok (twin islands with pristine coral reefs), Koh Ha (five small islands with excellent diving and snorkelling), and Koh Talabeng.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkelling at the marine park — the coral reefs here are among the most pristine in the Andaman Sea. Look out for sea turtles, reef sharks, and colourful tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a Thai massage on the beach (approx. 300–400 THB per hour) or simply unwind with a cocktail at a beachfront bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or bungalow breakfast — most mid-range accommodations on Koh Lanta offer breakfast packages (approx. 150–200 THB if not included).
meals.lunch: Included in the marine park tour — typically a Thai lunch served on one of the islands or on the boat.
meals.dinner: Mango House Restaurant near Long Beach — a cosy spot known for fresh seafood and Thai curries. Try the yellow curry with crab or grilled squid. Budget approx. 250–400 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok and Koh Ha tours cost approx. 1,200–1,800 THB per person including lunch and snorkelling equipment. Book the evening before. These are some of Thailand's best snorkelling spots — highly recommended. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Mu Ko Lanta National Park on the southern tip of Koh Lanta. Hike through jungle trails to a lighthouse with sweeping sea views. Look for monitor lizards, hornbills, and macaques along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Klong Nin Beach or Bamboo Bay — quieter and more secluded beaches on Koh Lanta's west coast. Swim, relax, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere away from the main tourist areas.
day_by_day.evening: Travel back north toward Long Beach and enjoy a final Koh Lanta evening. Visit a local night market if one is running, or enjoy a beachside bonfire dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit smoothie bowl and toast at a beachside café near your accommodation (approx. 100–180 THB).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local market or eat at a small local restaurant near Klong Nin Beach — try a simple pad see ew or fried rice (approx. 80–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Same Same But Different Bar & Restaurant — a popular Koh Lanta spot with a great menu of Thai and fusion dishes, live music, and a relaxed vibe. Budget approx. 200–350 THB per person.

day_by_day.notes: National park entry fee is approx. 200 THB per person. Wear sturdy shoes for the jungle hike. The lighthouse area can be muddy after rain — October is the shoulder season so light showers are possible. Bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — take the ferry from Koh Lanta back to Krabi, then connect to Phuket by minivan or bus (total travel time approx. 3–4 hours). Check in to a mid-range hotel in Patong Beach or Kata Beach area in Phuket.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, head to Kata Beach or Karon Beach for a relaxed afternoon swim. These are calmer and more family-friendly alternatives to Patong. Rent a sun lounger and enjoy the Andaman views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Patong's famous Bangla Road and the surrounding area for the classic Phuket nightlife experience. Even if nightlife isn't your priority, the street food and entertainment are worth seeing.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure from Koh Lanta — grab a banana roti from a street vendor (approx. 40–80 THB).
meals.lunch: Eat in Krabi Town during your connection — try a bowl of boat noodles or a quick pad thai at a market stall (approx. 80–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Patong Street Food — the side streets off Bangla Road are packed with excellent food stalls. Try grilled seafood, papaya salad, and mango sticky rice. Budget approx. 150–250 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Koh Lanta to Krabi ferry and onward minivan as a combined ticket — many tour desks offer this. Arrive in Phuket by early afternoon to maximise your beach time. Kata Beach is quieter than Patong and recommended for a more relaxed feel.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Phang Nga Bay — depart from Phuket by speedboat or longtail. Visit the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), Koh Panyi floating Muslim fishing village, and the dramatic limestone karsts rising from the emerald bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phuket by early afternoon. Visit the Big Buddha of Phuket — a 45-metre marble statue atop Nakkerd Hill with panoramic views of southern Phuket. Then explore Phuket Old Town's colourful Sino-Portuguese architecture and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Sunday Walking Street Market in Phuket Old Town (if visiting on a Sunday) or the Chillva Market for a fantastic street food experience with live music and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local kopitiam (coffee shop) in Phuket Town — try kaya toast with soft-boiled eggs and Thai iced coffee (approx. 80–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Koh Panyi village lunch — the floating village has numerous seafood restaurants. Try fresh grilled prawns and steamed fish with rice (approx. 200–300 THB).
meals.dinner: Phuket Old Town Street Food at Chillva Market or Lard Yai Walking Street — sample a wide variety of southern Thai dishes including mee hokkien, o-tao (oyster omelette), and coconut ice cream. Budget approx. 150–250 THB.

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay tours cost approx. 1,000–1,800 THB per person depending on boat type and inclusions. The Big Buddha is free to enter but donations are appreciated — dress modestly. Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last swim at your Phuket beach. Visit a local market one last time to pick up souvenirs: Thai silk scarves, elephant pants, local spices, and packaged Thai snacks make great gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final Thai massage at a reputable spa in Phuket (approx. 300–500 THB for 1 hour) or revisit a favourite beach spot. Begin packing and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Phuket International Airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your scheduled departure. Enjoy one last Thai meal at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a full Thai breakfast at a nice café — try a khao tom (rice soup) with side dishes, or a full American breakfast at your hotel. Budget approx. 150–250 THB.
meals.lunch: Final street food lunch near your hotel — pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) with a fried egg over rice is the perfect last Thai meal (approx. 80–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Phuket International Airport — options include local Thai restaurants and international chains. Budget approx. 200–400 THB for a sit-down meal before your flight.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 1.5–2 hours for the drive from Patong/Kata to Phuket Airport depending on traffic. Check out of your hotel by 12:00 noon (standard checkout) and store luggage if needed. Keep some Thai Baht for last-minute purchases and tips. Confirm your return flight details the night before.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Krabi pier, followed by a luxury speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to your boutique stay, unwind on the private terrace, and enjoy a welcome cocktail with panoramic sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along Phi Phi Don's Tonsai Village waterfront. Explore the vibrant night bazaar and sample local street food snacks including mango sticky rice and grilled skewers.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or light airport dining
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi — a beloved fine-casual spot known for fresh seafood, Thai curries, and wood-fired dishes in a cozy garden setting.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private speedboat transfer in advance for comfort and efficiency. October marks the tail end of the rainy season — expect occasional showers but fewer crowds and lush scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat tour to Maya Bay (The Beach) at sunrise for an exclusive early-access experience before day-trippers arrive. Snorkel in the crystal-clear waters of Loh Samah Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Island hop to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) — a pristine, less-visited island with powdery white sand and turquoise shallows. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by your resort on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don. Enjoy a traditional Thai cooking class at a boutique culinary studio, learning to prepare tom kha gai, pad thai, and green curry from scratch.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at your boutique resort featuring tropical fruits, eggs benedict, fresh juices, and Thai congee.
meals.lunch: Private beach picnic — curated charcuterie, fresh fruit, Thai wraps, and sparkling water arranged by the resort.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cosmic Restaurant, Phi Phi — rooftop dining with panoramic ocean views, serving elevated Thai and Mediterranean fusion cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Book Maya Bay early-access permits in advance as visitor numbers are strictly controlled to protect the ecosystem. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Guided kayaking tour through the dramatic limestone karsts and hidden lagoons of Phi Phi Leh. Explore sea caves and emerald-green coves accessible only by kayak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at your resort's infinity pool or private beach. Optional: book a 90-minute traditional Thai massage and aromatherapy session at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Phi Phi Don fire show night — head to Tonsai Bay beachfront to watch world-class fire dancers perform. Enjoy cocktails at a premium beach bar.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — avocado toast, smoked salmon, fresh papaya, and cold-pressed juices.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Papaya Restaurant, Phi Phi — fresh spring rolls, som tum (papaya salad), and coconut smoothies.
meals.dinner: Seafood barbecue dinner at Phi Phi Viewpoint Restaurant — grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and whole snapper with panoramic hillside views.

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking tours typically depart at 8:00 AM to catch calm morning waters. Confirm spa bookings the evening prior.

day_by_day.morning: Hike to Phi Phi Viewpoint — a 30-minute trail rewarding you with one of Southeast Asia's most iconic twin-bay panoramas. Ideal for photography at golden hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat day trip to Koh Yao Noi — a serene, largely undeveloped island in Phang Nga Bay. Cycle through rice paddies, rubber plantations, and traditional Muslim fishing villages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi. Enjoy a private sunset dinner cruise around the islands aboard a chartered catamaran, with a private chef serving a five-course Thai tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the hike — yogurt parfait, granola, tropical fruits, and Thai iced coffee.
meals.lunch: Local lunch on Koh Yao Noi at a family-run restaurant — fresh fish curry, jasmine rice, and stir-fried morning glory.
meals.dinner: Five-course private chef dinner aboard a sunset catamaran cruise — champagne, fresh ceviche, lobster bisque, grilled sea bass, and mango sorbet.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy footwear for the viewpoint hike. The catamaran dinner cruise must be booked at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Speedboat transfer to Krabi Town. Visit Wat Tham Seua (Tiger Cave Temple) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking views over Krabi's jungle and coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Krabi Town's famous Chao Fa Weekend Market area and the riverside promenade. Visit local artisan shops and browse handmade crafts, silk scarves, and Thai ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Street food evening in Krabi Town — indulge in authentic local delicacies at the night market including pad see ew, boat noodles, roti with condensed milk, and fresh coconut ice cream.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure — full Thai breakfast with rice soup, fried eggs, and fresh tropical fruit.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ruen Mai Restaurant, Krabi — one of Krabi's most respected Thai restaurants, known for authentic southern Thai cuisine and royal recipes.
meals.dinner: Street food feast at Krabi Town Night Market — budget-friendly yet authentic; pair with fresh coconut water and Thai iced tea.

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb takes approximately 45–60 minutes each way. Start early to avoid midday heat. Dress modestly as it is an active place of worship.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Four Islands tour departing from Krabi — visit Koh Poda, Koh Gai (Chicken Island), Koh Tub, and Koh Mor by private longtail boat. Snorkel, swim, and walk the sandbar connecting the islands at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands tour with a stop at Thale Waek (Separated Sea) — a magical sandbar that appears at low tide linking two islands. Ideal for photography and wading.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Islands via private speedboat. Enjoy a relaxed evening at your boutique resort with in-room dining and a bottle of fine wine from the resort's curated cellar.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — continental spread with pastries, fruit, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box provided for the boat tour — sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy bars, and bottled water.
meals.dinner: In-room private dining experience — resort chef prepares a personalized Thai tasting menu delivered to your villa or terrace.

day_by_day.notes: Sandbar timing is tide-dependent — confirm low tide times with your tour operator the evening before. Bring waterproof bags for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the beach, arranged by the resort. Followed by a guided snorkeling session at the nearby coral-rich waters of Phi Phi's Hin Klang reef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon for leisure — relax by the pool, read on the beach, or explore Phi Phi's boutique shops for souvenirs, handmade jewelry, and local artwork.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's ocean-facing bar. Dinner at a premium restaurant on the island.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga smoothie bowls and avocado toast at the resort's beach café.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ciao Bella, Phi Phi — Italian-Thai fusion with fresh pasta, seafood risotto, and wood-fired pizza overlooking the bay.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Phi Phi The Beach Resort's Horizon Restaurant — candlelit beachfront dining with a focus on locally sourced seafood and Thai herbs.

day_by_day.notes: Yoga sessions can be arranged through the resort concierge. October waters are generally calm and excellent for snorkeling despite being shoulder season.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat transfer to Koh Lanta — a quieter, more laid-back island south of Phi Phi. Visit the Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a charming 100-year-old Sino-Portuguese fishing village with wooden stilt houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mu Ko Lanta National Park — hike through mangrove forests, spot wildlife, and relax at the secluded Hat Nui beach within the park. Optional cave exploration at Khao Mai Kaew caves.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at one of Koh Lanta's famous Long Beach sunset bars. Enjoy a seafood dinner before the private boat returns to Phi Phi.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure — full buffet with made-to-order eggs and fresh juices.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Time for Lime, Koh Lanta — a celebrated culinary school and restaurant offering authentic Thai dishes in a lush garden setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lanta Seafood Restaurant on the beachfront — whole grilled barracuda, steamed clams in lemongrass broth, and coconut pudding for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the return speedboat to depart no later than 19:30 to ensure a safe nighttime crossing. Koh Lanta's Old Town is best explored on foot or by rented bicycle.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive Phang Nga Bay day trip by private luxury speedboat — explore the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), towering limestone karsts, and the floating Muslim village of Koh Panyee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayak through Phang Nga Bay's ethereal sea caves and hidden hongs (interior lagoons) accessible only at low tide. A guide will lead you through these magical enclosed spaces.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi. Enjoy a traditional Thai herbal steam bath and full-body massage at the resort spa — the perfect recovery after an active day.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — Thai-style rice porridge, fresh fruit, and strong Thai coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Koh Panyee floating village — fresh crab curry and grilled fish at one of the stilted restaurants over the water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at your resort — chef's special five-course tasting menu featuring southern Thai flavors, paired with selected wines.

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay is a full-day excursion — depart by 7:30 AM. The hong kayaking is tide-dependent; your guide will manage the timing. Bring a dry bag and camera.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast, swim in the ocean, or take a paddleboard session along the coastline. Alternatively, join a guided birdwatching walk through Phi Phi's forested interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scuba diving experience with a certified dive master — explore the vibrant coral reefs and diverse marine life around Phi Phi, including the famous King Cruiser Wreck dive site (for certified divers).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail hour at the resort's sunset terrace. Enjoy a final premium dinner on Phi Phi Island.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — eggs royale, smoked salmon bagel, fresh-pressed green juice, and cappuccino.
meals.lunch: Post-dive lunch at Phi Phi Natural Resort's beachside restaurant — light Thai noodles, fresh coconut, and tropical fruit platter.
meals.dinner: Gala dinner at Phi Phi Island Village Beach Resort's signature restaurant — seven-course royal Thai banquet with live traditional music performance.

day_by_day.notes: Scuba diving certification is required for the King Cruiser Wreck dive. Beginners can opt for a Discover Scuba Diving intro session in shallower reef areas instead.

day_by_day.morning: Check out from Phi Phi boutique stay. Private speedboat transfer to Phuket. Check in to a luxury Phuket resort (Banyan Tree, Amanpuri, or similar). Freshen up and explore the resort grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-recognized heritage area with beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture, colorful shophouses, and vibrant street art. Explore Thalang Road and Soi Rommanee.
day_by_day.evening: Street food tour of Phuket Town with a private guide — taste local specialties including Hokkien noodles, o-tao (oyster omelette), mee sua, and the famous Phuket lobster satay.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Phi Phi boutique resort before checkout.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kopitiam by Wilai, Phuket Old Town — an iconic local eatery serving authentic Peranakan-Thai dishes in a heritage shophouse setting.
meals.dinner: Street food evening tour through Phuket Town's night market — a curated tasting journey of 8–10 local dishes with a private guide.

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The private street food tour can be arranged through your new resort's concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Big Buddha (Phra Phutta Ming Mongkol Akenakkiri) on Nakkerd Hill — a 45-meter marble statue offering 360-degree views of Phuket. Explore nearby Wat Chalong temple complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon at Kata Noi or Surin Beach — two of Phuket's most beautiful and upscale beaches. Enjoy a beachside cabana with butler service at a premium beach club.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at Baba Nest rooftop bar at Sri Panwa resort — consistently rated one of Asia's best rooftop bars with 360-degree panoramic views. Followed by a lavish dinner.

meals.breakfast: Luxury resort breakfast — international buffet with live cooking stations, pastries, tropical fruits, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Catch Beach Club, Surin Beach — Mediterranean-Thai menu with fresh seafood, lobster rolls, and wood-fired dishes on the sand.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Acqua Restaurant, Phuket — award-winning Italian fine dining with ocean views, featuring handmade pasta, Wagyu beef, and an extensive wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly at religious sites (cover shoulders and knees). Baba Nest rooftop bar is extremely popular — reservations are essential and must be made well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning leisure — enjoy a last swim, spa treatment, or sunrise beach walk. Pack and check out of the Phuket resort. Private transfer to Phuket International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure preparations — airport shopping for last-minute Thai souvenirs, premium Thai silk, artisan coffee, and snacks. Enjoy the airport lounge before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry beautiful memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring Thailand's finest beaches, islands, and culinary landscape.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — choose your favorites from the menu as a farewell meal.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport's premium lounge or a quick bite at a quality airport restaurant.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at a layover destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport check-in and immigration. Keep a small Thai baht reserve for last-minute purchases. Consider purchasing vacuum-sealed Thai curry pastes and premium jasmine rice as gourmet souvenirs.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
